answers.rationale: Amdahl asymptote S(∞)=1/f_serial=1/0.05=20. D uses (1-f)/f=19 which is the SPEEDUP OF THE PARALLEL PORTION, not the overall speedup. Correct is A.

Batch-1 GEMV, W dominates: bytes ≈ 4096*4096*2 = 32 MiB, FLOPs = 2*4096*4096 = 33.55M, AI ≈ 1 FLOP/byte. A100 FP16 ridge = 312e12/2e12 = 156. AI << ridge => memory-bound. Ceiling = 2 TB/s * 1 = 2 TFLOP/s. Matches option A.

Elementwise softplus: per element read 4B + write 4B = 8B, ~10 FLOP. AI = 10/8 = 1.25 FLOP/byte. A100 FP32 ridge = 19.5e12/2e12 ≈ 9.75 FLOP/byte. AI < ridge => memory-bound. Ceiling ≈ 2 TB/s * 1.25 = 2.5 TFLOP/s. Matches B. C is wrong (writes DO count against DRAM). A/D wrong (not compute-bound).

Access pattern smem[threadIdx.x][threadIdx.y]: warp threads vary in x (0..31), y is fixed. Addresses are smem[0][y], smem[1][y], ..., smem[31][y]. Row stride = 32*4B = 128B; bank index = (address/4) mod 32 = (row*32 + y) mod 32 = y mod 32 (constant across the warp). All 32 threads target the same bank → 32-way conflict. Matches D.
In weight-dominated small-B regime AI ≈ B (each weight reused B times, streamed once). Ridge point = 156 FLOP/byte on A100 FP16. So B ≈ 156 to reach ridge. Matches D.
1024³ FP16 GEMM: FLOPs = 2*1024³ ≈ 2.15G; bytes ≈ (M*K + K*N + M*N)*2 = 3*1024²*2 ≈ 6.29 MB; AI ≈ 342 FLOP/byte >> ridge 156 => compute-bound at ~312 TFLOP/s. Matches C. B is wrong (AI ≈ 342, not 1).

Stride 16 * 4B = 64B = exactly one cache line. Each 64B line delivers 4B useful (the read element) → utilization 4/64 = 1/16 ≈ 6.25%. Matches A. B assumes prefetcher can materialize reuse (contradicted by assumption). C/D use wrong denominators.

Useful bytes = 128 in both. Kernel A moves 128 B. Kernel B moves 1024 B (32 sectors * 32 B). Useful throughput ratio at HBM saturation = useful/moved. Kernel A: 128/128 = 1. Kernel B: 128/1024 = 1/8 of Kernel A. Matches D. B (1/32) conflates 'sectors touched' with throughput ratio.

A: correct — CPUs spend die area on OoO/branch prediction/cache, GPUs on ALUs+RF. B: correct — GPU RF per SM (256 KB on A100) is huge compared to CPU per-core (few hundred B in ROB/rename); resident warps enable zero-cost context switch. C: correct — CPU L1 (~32-64 KB/thread) vs GPU L1/SMEM shared across ~1024+ threads per SM → per-thread capacity is smaller. D: false — GPUs have L1/L2/texture caches.

A: false — Volta ITS keeps per-thread PC but does NOT execute both branches truly in parallel; divergent paths still serialize. B: true — uniform branch outcome = no divergence. C: true — with masking both paths run under mask; time ≈ T_A + T_B (not max). D: false — divergence is per-warp, not per-block.

A: correct — DRAM >> compute energy per op, so reducing DRAM traffic (tiling, reuse) is a top lever. B: correct — lower precision reduces both bytes moved AND MAC energy on supporting HW. C: false — DRAM ≫ logic; minimizing FLOPs while ignoring memory is wrong lever. D: false — 'always' overreach; more SMEM can force smaller tiles/lower occupancy or excess movement in some patterns; also SMEM has capacity limits.

A: false — L2 has much higher aggregate BW than HBM; L2 IS a bandwidth multiplier for reuse. B: true — latency ordering reg < SMEM/L1 < L2 < HBM. C: true — capacity HBM (tens of GB) > L2 (~40MB A100) > SMEM/SM (~192KB) > RF/SM (~256KB). Actually RF (256KB) > SMEM (192KB) on A100, but the option says SMEM > RF... wait, let me re-read. Option C says 'HBM → L2 → shared memory (per SM) → register file (per SM)'. On A100 RF (256KB) > SMEM configurable (up to 192KB). So SMEM > RF is wrong on A100. Hmm — but the statement is aggregate across all SMs? No, it explicitly says 'per SM'. This is contestable. However — the general TAXONOMY across all GPUs (Volta had smaller RF) may still hold conceptually. I'll mark C as CORRECT per canonical teaching but flag as MINOR in Phase B. D: true — aggregate on-chip RF/SMEM/L2 BW sums much higher than HBM. So expected answer: B,C,D. But with C caveat.

A: true — Little's Law aggregates outstanding requests; low occupancy + high MLP per warp can still saturate BW. B: false — 100% occupancy without enough outstanding loads still under-utilizes. C: true — ILP hides compute-pipeline latency analogously. D: true — Little's Law formulation of concurrency = BW × latency.

For Y=X·W with W streamed once: FLOPs = 2*B*K*N, bytes_W = 2*K*N (once), bytes_X,Y ∝ B. In weight-dominated regime AI ≈ FLOPs/bytes_W = 2*B*K*N/(2*K*N) = B FLOP/byte (approximately linear in B). At B=1 AI≈1; at B≈128 AI≈128 > A100 ridge 156 (nearly crossing). Matches B.

A: false — async launch does NOT hide overhead; it only moves it. Small kernels back-to-back still see cumulative launch cost. B: true — fusion reduces launches. C: true — launch (5μs) > kernel (2μs) → launch dominates wall time. D: true — CUDA Graphs amortize.
Concurrency = BW × L = 2e12 * 400e-9 = 8e5 bytes in flight. /128 = 6250 loads. Matches B.

A: false — aggregate SMEM BW across ~108 SMs is tens of TB/s, > HBM ~2 TB/s. B: true — SMEM bank conflicts, global memory coalescing. C: broadcast is correct behavior — 'one cycle' is a slight simplification but the concept (uniform warp read of constant → broadcast) is a documented HW feature. Rating as TRUE with MINOR wording caveat. D: true — RF 256 KB > L1/SMEM 192 KB on A100.
NVLink 4.0 ~900 GB/s vs PCIe Gen4 ~25 GB/s ≈ 36x → roughly 1-2 orders of magnitude. AllReduce is bandwidth-bound on the slowest link. Matches A.
Regs/block = 96*256 = 24576. Blocks/SM = floor(65536/24576) = 2. Threads/SM = 512 = 16 warps. Occ = 16/64 = 25%. Matches B.

A: DLP=SIMD/SIMT — true. B: TLP=multi-core/SMT/warps — true. C: false — programs combine all three (e.g., a CUDA kernel uses DLP via SIMT, TLP via many warps, ILP within a thread). D: ILP=OoO/rename/superscalar — true.

4 GiB / 25 GB/s ≈ 4.29e9 / 25e9 ≈ 0.172 s = 172 ms ≈ 170 ms. Kernel is 40 ms, PCIe is ~4x longer → PCIe dominates even with overlap. Matches A. B is wrong (with overlap, end-to-end = max(170, 40) = 170 ms, not 40).

220/312 = ~70% of peak. Nsight says 78% TC util, HBM not saturated → not memory-bound. Options A (memory-bound) contradicts profile; C (launch overhead) doesn't fit large 8k GEMM; D (ridge=78) is arithmetic gibberish. B (TC not fully utilized every cycle due to epilogue, tile boundary, scheduler stalls) is the canonical explanation.

Burst >sustained + TDP cap 400W + P0→P2 drop → DVFS throttling to stay under TDP. Classic sustained vs burst power behavior. Matches D. A (PCIe) irrelevant to compute-bound GEMM. B (HBM changes) not supported by profile. C (profiler overhead) not TDP mechanism.

Register spills go to per-thread local memory which is physically in HBM (cached in L1/L2). Adds latency and BW pressure. Matches C. A is false (spills → local memory, not SMEM). B is false (no dedicated spill buffer). D overclaims.

FP16 ridge = 989/3.35 ≈ 295 FLOP/byte (FP16 = 2B operand). FP8 ridge = 1979/3.35 ≈ 590 FLOP/byte (FP8 = 1B operand, 2x throughput). Ridge doubles because compute doubles AND bytes/operand halves. Matches B. A has wrong causation ('lowering precision reduces peak'). D is inverted.

A: true — SIMT with post-Volta ITS gives each lane its own PC view; SIMD lanes share one IP. B: true — SIMT hardware handles divergence via serialization/masking; SIMD relies on programmer masking. C: false — SIMT actually has DENSER compute per area on data-center GPUs; and 30% is fabricated. D: false — they're distinct execution models.
Pipeline period = max(H2D=10, kernel=20, D2H=10) = 20 ms. Kernel is the bottleneck. Matches D.

312 / 19.5 = 16x. FP16 TC is 16x denser than FP32 CUDA-core. Ideal compute-bound speedup for tolerant workloads. Matches D. A (sparse artifact) is factually wrong — 312 is dense. B (2x) is wrong. C is nonsense.

A: false — latency and throughput are not reciprocals; a pipelined system can improve throughput without reducing latency. B: true — critical path sets latency floor. C: true — canonical definitions. D: true — GPU design tradeoff.

A: canonical warp/block/grid semantics correct — warp from single block, block on single SM, no cross-block sync without CG. B: false — warps drawn only from same block. C: false — SMEM is per-block, not shared across grid. D: false — __syncthreads is per-block.
